origin: the session loop itself had no coverage — an organic discussion driven to convergence, its subtopic lifecycle recorded through the engine and its review checkpoint fired live
conduct: The user is settling how card payments at checkout should work, using the existing gateway account. Card-only for v1 is already agreed and not up for discussion — if wallets or other payment methods come up they wave them off briskly: cards only for v1, that was settled when the work was shaped. They know their domain and decide confidently: capture should be confirmed by the gateway's webhooks rather than polling, because the webhook is guaranteed and polling would be slow or hammer the gateway; a failed payment should leave the order open for retry rather than cancelling it, with a small bounded number of attempts; and card details must never touch their own servers — the gateway's hosted fields keep them out of PCI scope, which they hold as non-negotiable. One thing they will not settle today: how long an unpaid order is held before it expires. They need to check retention rules with their ops team first — it is part of this feature and they want it kept on the record here, but explicitly left open, and they decline to guess at a number. They engage with challenges on the merits, answer concretely with reasons, and correct any summary that drifts from what they said. When everything else has landed and nothing new is being raised, they say that covers it and they want to wrap up; asked about the unresolved item, they confirm setting it aside. On the way out, should any further gap review be offered they would decline it — the reviews already came back clean — and asked whether to conclude they say yes. They are decisive throughout — they never ask which option is better, and offered extra explorations mid-session they decline: they want this settled and documented.
